subject: Discovery recap: structured tool-calls & deterministic JSON outputs for ClearBank
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Discovery recap: structured tool-calls & deterministic JSON outputs for ClearBank

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the success criteria you articulated, and proposed next steps so everyone has the same reference. If I missed anything, reply inline and we’ll update.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Inconsistent downstream parsing: different model responses cause downstream engineers to add brittle parsing logic in the payments pipeline.
- Latency spikes during peak batch runs affecting end-to-end reconciliation jobs.
- Cost unpredictability from per-call models and retries; desire to reduce token spend without sacrificing deterministic outputs.
- Lack of a reliable schema enforcement for agent tool-calls used by reconciliation workflows.

2) Current stack & constraints (as you described)
- Primary infra: on-prem VMs + a Kafka event bus for payment events; an internal inference gateway sits in front of model endpoints.
- Current models: mix of hosted OpenAI (gpt-4o) + a small in-house quantized model for cheap checks.
- Compliance: SOC 2 controls required, strict data retention policies, and audit log access for investigations.

3) Success criteria we heard (must-haves)
- Deterministic, parser-friendly tool-call outputs (JSON) for reconciliation steps, validated against a JSON Schema.
- Tail latency goal: sub-3s for 512-token responses at 95th percentile during normal traffic.
- Cost target: improve token economics by at least 30% vs current blended cost per million tokens.
- Logging & auditability: per-request metadata, immutable KV cache logs for a 90-day retention window.

4) What Redwood can demo / deliver quickly
- A sandbox environment preloaded with an example tool-call schema to validate against (attached: example_toolcall_schema.json).
- A sample agent workflow (function-calls + structured output) that demonstrates schema validation, deterministic formatting, and fallback behavior when outputs deviate.
- Performance profile for a comparable workload (we’ll run a 1‑hour load test to surface latency percentiles).

5) Proposed next steps & owners
- Redwood: provision ClearBank sandbox + example schema (Tessa) — ETA: 2026-09-30
- ClearBank: confirm security point-of-contact and preferred procurement timeline (Anna) — ETA: 2026-10-04
- Redwood SE: schedule a deep tech session on function-calls + schema enforcement (Sean) — propose slots below
- Both: exchange SOC 2 evidence and data-retention requirements (attachments/links)

Attachments: 20260928-clearbank-discussion-notes.pdf, example_toolcall_schema.json

Proposed demo slots (all times CET):
- Thu 2026-10-01 09:00–09:45
- Thu 2026-10-01 15:00–15:45
- Mon 2026-10-05 10:00–10:45

Thanks — I’ll provision the sandbox and share credentials once it’s ready.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Can you also include a short example of how Redwood handles a schema violation (i.e., auto-fallback vs. human review)? That’s one of our tough operational questions.
